rules.text: After touching `data/` or `schemas/` you must run: `cargo run --example pack -- .ygg/mods/pi-agent-seed`.

Lua static checks: `cargo run -p ygg-lint -- --pack .ygg/mods/pi-agent-seed` (whole-pack mode, which also validates the `code.modules` declarations) or `cargo run -p ygg-lint -- .ygg/mods/pi-agent-seed/mod.lua` (single-file mode); the result must be 0 errors / 0 warnings.

Smoke walk: `cargo run --example playtest -- .ygg/mods/pi-agent-seed` (the all-1 walk must reach `[ENDING`). All-1 covers the happy path only — the acceptance standard for branches and map wording is `gates.mod-semantics-matrix` (`cargo test -p ygg-sandbox --test agent_seed_semantics`).
The manifest is content-addressed (sha256 + byteLength): editing `data/*.json` without recomputing the pack makes loading fail with a content-hash mismatch.

A multi-file Mod is registered only in the `code` section of `pack.json`: `entry` is not registered as a module, `modules` enumerates every file explicitly (no glob), and a missing `code` section means a single-file Mod (no migration needed for existing Mods). `require` works both at load time and at runtime (inside a handler) — `host.seal` only seals `ygg.on`, so a pure library may be loaded lazily; the price is that a module's top level may be a pure export surface only (see `harness.module-pure-export`). After changing any module file you must rerun pack (content-addressed: a byte-count or hash mismatch fails loading).
rules.basis: docs/DESIGN.md §3.2 "multi-file Mod" (the r5 documentation surface; the same-named subsection expands each item)

rules.text: A multi-file Mod's module chunk performs pure exports only (function and constant definitions) and does nothing with side effects: registration / state writes / output all live in the entry `mod.lua`. A module exposes registration as a function (`function M.install(deps)`) that the entry calls explicitly in order; touching `ygg.on` / `ygg.emit` / `ygg.narrate` / `ygg.choice` / `ygg.meta` / `ygg.kv.set` / `ygg.entity.spawn` / `ygg.entity.set_attribute` / `ygg.entity.add_tag` / `ygg.entity.remove_tag` / `ygg.fsm.define` / `ygg.narrative.node` / `ygg.narrative["goto"]` at a module's top level is refused (the static `YGG-MOD-EFFECT` rule and the runtime shadow table share the single list `ygg_modules::effects`); at the top level only pure reads are allowed (`ygg.data` / `ygg.ticks` / `ygg.kv.get` / `ygg.entity.has_tag` / `ygg.entity.get_attribute`); the entry chunk is exempt (it is the assembly manifest). Why: a handler's dispatch order equals the `ygg.on` registration order — letting a module register itself means "how the files are split / who is required first" decides runtime behavior, so splitting a file or reordering a `require` would change the dispatch order and refactoring would not preserve behavior. `require` is therefore usable at any time (including lazy-loading a pure library inside a handler), but lazy loading never relaxes the boundary: a lazily loaded module's top level is still pure exports. See `docs/DESIGN.md` §3.2 "Mod Package & Multi-File Purity Contract".
rules.basis: docs/DESIGN.md §3.2 "multi-file Mod", side-effect boundary (semantics tightened in r1/r2/r3; the single source for both lists is ygg_modules::effects)

rules.text: In a multi-file Mod the KV prefixes are partitioned by ownership and each prefix has exactly one writer (a documentation convention; loading does not validate it): `fsm.*` is written only by the stdlib `ygg.fsm` and read-only for the Mod; `settings.*` is written only by `config.set`; `req.*` = the requirement table, `prop.*` = the proposal table, `lane.*` = the lane ledger, `ui.*` = presentation only (never in the summary, never affecting dispatch), and `task.*` / `verify.*` / `review.*` / `inbox.*` plus the bare key `ending` each have their own single writer. Two modules writing one prefix is implicit coupling — share through a module's return value instead.
rules.basis: docs/DESIGN.md §3.2 "KV prefix ownership" (user decision: documentation convention only, no load-time validation surface)

rules.text: Never "glue a multi-file Mod back into one file and then report errors": a module chunk name must carry the real file (`@src/core/util.lua`), a refusal the loader decides itself must carry the call site (`src/a.lua:3: <reason>`) and the require chain, and static checks must parse each module independently (a module's `local` never spans chunks, so gluing would invent a shared scope that does not exist at load time). A diagnostic whose line number does not match the real file is a defect.
rules.basis: docs/DESIGN.md §3.2 "error location: real file + real line number"

rules.text: Hot reload: single-shot mode loads from disk in every new process; a `--resume` receipt with `hotReload.source="resume"` proves the change is in effect.

The two Mods are a division of labor (not the same file): the skeleton surface (`mod.lua` + `schemas/`) is byte-identical and kept in sync by `scripts/sync-seed-mod.sh` (CI has a skeleton guard); the instance surface `data/` is maintained on each side — `packages/mods/pi-agent-seed` is the distributable seed template (5 generic chapters, zero project rules) and `.ygg/mods/pi-agent-seed` is this project's instance (14 chapters, this one included).
